issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for assembleBookstore(): The problem statement (and the template's commented stub) specify a parameterless factory function assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore that the client should implement. In the solution repository, the Client.main() call invokes assembleBookstore() with no arguments (call site at Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift line 5), but the solution defines private static func assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore (definition at Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift line 31), i.e. requiring a Bool parameter. This mismatch (call vs. declaration) will cause a compilation error and confuses students about the required signature to implement and test.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore function signature consistent with the problem statement and template. Change the solution declaration to a parameterless function: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } so the call assembleBookstore() in main() compiles. Alternatively, if a parameter was intentional, update the template and problem statement to require assembleBookstore(check: Bool) and update all call sites to pass a default or explicit Bool (e.g. add a default value check: Bool = false).
